cases.public_brief:
Step through transcript events with the left and right arrow keys

In the offline viewer from #6, a reader inspecting a vote should be able to step through the transcript while keeping their eyes on the floor plan.

- Left Arrow goes back one event. Right Arrow advances one. Reuse the existing navigation in `footsteps/web/viewer.js` so the floor, ballots, event log, and slider stay in sync.
- Stop at the first and last events. Preserve native arrow-key behavior in the turn selector, tile selector, and range input. In particular, one press on the focused slider should move exactly once. Preserve keyboard focus as the view updates.
- Make the shortcuts discoverable alongside the existing playback controls.

Verify with the offline export of `examples/crossing.json`. From event 4, press Right to reveal the tied ballot and move the marker to (1, 0). Press Left to restore the pending proposal and the marker at (0, 0). Also check both endpoints and the focused controls. This task can ship independently of changes to how a transcript is opened.

Keep focus on the same usable control when navigating, including a floor tile button if its tile still exists. When a tile disappears or a focused playback button becomes disabled, choose a usable playback or inspection control. Browser acceptance is checked independently. You can exercise the supplied Python viewer tests; identify any browser checks you cannot run.
cases.blind_review:
Blind interpretation of the public assignment

The index includes setup at 0. An unmodified Left or Right key on the page, a floor button, or a playback button requests one step through the existing go function. At an endpoint the index stays fixed. Each selector and the range input retain their native behavior, including their existing change and input handlers. A visible indication on each playback control identifies its shortcut.

The floor rebuilds every button on each update. A tile's coordinate identifies the same tile across frames even when its marker or proposal label changes. A surviving focused tile must remain reachable in the fixed-size floor window. Focus may move to a usable inspection or playback control if its former target disappears or becomes disabled.

The brief leaves fallback control selection open. This submission uses the tile picker for a removed tile and the opposite playback button for a disabled button. I interpret Left and Right as unmodified keys and preserve modified shortcuts for the browser. The approach is feasible within the allowed paths. I found no substantive contract gap.

cases.public_brief:
Import the final game block when a full Markdown account includes an earlier example

The full account format defines a labeled JSON block at the end of the Markdown file as the importable record. Adding a quoted example with the same fence label earlier in the editable prose breaks import. Found during #26 at f5625da.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from footsteps.record import read, render

record = read("examples/crossing.json")
intro = "An example of the block syntax:\n```json footsteps-record\n{}\n```\n\n"
with TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    p = Path(tmp) / "worked.md"
    p.write_text(intro + render(record, full=True))
    assert read(p) == record
```

Observed: ValueError: malformed full account. The parser split at the first labeled fence. The final block is the original, valid crossing record.

Done when both replay and view can read this full account, and the reader still rejects a truncated final block or trailing non-whitespace after it. Cover an incorrect final block after an earlier valid one so the importer cannot silently replay an earlier example. No format version change is needed.

Add standard-library regression tests in tests/test_record_import.py. Keep ordinary JSON and the documented full Markdown format working. The CLI uses read for both commands; the selected workspace includes its reader and viewer functions. The Maintainer also checks the full CLI.
cases.blind_review:
The last exact opening label used by the existing renderer selects the JSON to import. An earlier labeled example in editable prose can contain unrelated data. Closing the selected block and consuming only whitespace through EOF are required. A bad final block must fail even after a valid example. Plain JSON decoding and the renderer's record format stay as specified.

The documentation and reproduction agree. The reader decodes JSON and replay validates game semantics. I interpret “incorrect final block” as covering invalid JSON, a missing close, and a non-whitespace suffix at the reader boundary. Semantically invalid JSON records continue through the existing replay validation. No substantive ambiguity or blocker identified. The selected files permit writing the implementation and exercising the replay renderer and transcript function. Full CLI verification requires the Maintainer's workspace.

limitations: Selected cases from one purpose-built project. Outcomes do not estimate transfer probability across projects or task families.
The hosted submissions were blind first attempts with different tools, no candidate execution before sealing, and no matched end-to-end timing.

Maintainer work included writing the isolated browser input replay, provisioning its fonts, checking the CLI, reviewing handoffs and preparing upstream pull requests. Attentive time was not metered; dispatch is elapsed time and overlaps other work.
decision: Delegate another bounded parser or record maintenance task with an existing fixture and cheap independent CLI replay. For browser behavior, pair delegation with an available native-key verifier and budget for recovering and reviewing saved code if the handoff is missing. These two outcomes do not justify changing the incumbent recipe or estimating a cross-repository pass rate.

full_autonomous_results.criterion: Artifact satisfies the original behavioral checks and an independently supported final handoff is present.
